question: Which of the following antibiotics could be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Piperacillin / tazobactam" -> "beta-lactam antibiotic" -> "cross-reactivity with penicillin" -> "not suitable for penicillin allergy" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Aztreonam" -> "monobactam antibiotic" -> "low cross-reactivity with penicillin" -> "suitable for penicillin allergy" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Ampicillin" -> "beta-lactam antibiotic" -> "high cross-reactivity with penicillin" -> "not suitable for penicillin allergy" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Amoxicillin" -> "beta-lactam antibiotic" -> "high cross-reactivity with penicillin" -> "not suitable for penicillin allergy" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Ceftazidime" -> "cephalosporin antibiotic" -> "possible cross-reactivity with penicillin" -> "unclear suitability for penicillin allergy" -> 50%
analysis: Aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic that is structurally different from penicillins and cephalosporins, and it is generally considered safe for use in patients with penicillin allergies. The other options listed are either penicillins or cephalosporins, which may cross-react in patients with penicillin hypersensitivity.
